reason: The cited evidence supports that two-step aging refines precipitates in Ti alloys (E1), sigma precipitates strengthen BCC HEAs at high temperatures (E2, E3), and Ti2Ni/sigma phases appear in Ti-Ni-Al HEAs (E4). However, no evidence directly demonstrates coherent Ti2Ni or sigma precipitation strengthening in a Ti-Ni-primary HEA, and the specific composition Ti35Ni35Cr10Al10Mo10 is unsupported.
premises: Two-step aging can produce fine, uniformly distributed precipitates in Ti alloys and HEAs
Sigma precipitates in BCC HEA matrices can enhance elevated-temperature yield strength
Ti2Ni or sigma phases can form in Ti-Ni-containing HEAs
Heat treatment at ~1100°C can produce sigma particles in refractory HEAs
Fine precipitates improve strength by acting as obstacles to dislocation motion
